meta.title: Game Model · Flexible 4-2-3-1 · Possession on Purpose
meta.notes:
Our game model: a flexible 4-2-3-1 that keeps the ball on purpose. Staggered support draws the opponent to the ball; we find the free player in the centre or a half-space, and once he faces forward we accelerate with combinations, forward passes or wide support.

Roles: deep-lying playmakers close to the centre-backs, deep fullbacks feeding inverted wingers in the half-spaces, the 10 in the right half-space beside the RW, the 9 on the blind side of a centre-back.

Sections: 01 The idea · 02 Identity · 03 Shape and roles · 04 Non-negotiables · 05 Patterns P1-P7 · 06 Training. Tap the current slide number for notes and contents.

items.text:
OUR GAME MODEL
Possession on purpose. A flexible
4-2-3-1: draw them in, find the
free man, face forward,
accelerate.

steps.title: 00 Introduction — Cover
steps.note:
The idea:
- A flexible 4-2-3-1 that keeps the ball on purpose. We use staggered support to draw the opponent towards the ball, find a free player in the centre or a half-space, and the moment he receives facing forward we accelerate towards goal: a combination, a forward pass or wide support.
- We build quickly from deep, overload the centre, disrupt their structure and progress mainly from the right, wide and inside.

Organisation:
- Section 01 The idea · 02 Identity · 03 Shape and roles · 04 Non-negotiables · 05 Patterns P1-P7 · 06 Training T1-T5 and the week.
- Every slide is animated and carries its own notes. Tap the current slide number for the notes and the contents; on a large screen the notes sit beside the pitch.
- Present it in tap mode: each tap plays the next picture, so you can talk the squad through one action at a time.

steps.title: 00 Introduction — How to read the diagrams
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Blue: our team. Red: the opponent, a 4-4-2 (S striker, WM wide midfielder, CM central midfielder, FB fullback, CB centre-back).
- We always attack to the right. Our left touchline is at the top of the screen.
- Arrows: white pass, orange our run, wavy carry, gold dashed their movement, solid gold their pass. Numbers on passes give the order. A hatched area is the space we want to use.
- The opponent is alive on every slide: their block slides to the ball, presses, tracks our runners and recovers. Watch the gold runs: every one of them leaves a space we attack.
- Each slide draws its arrows first, then the players move. In tap mode the next tap plays the next picture.

steps.title: 00 Introduction — Contents
steps.note:
Organisation:

items.text:
THE IDEA
Draw them in. Find the
free man. He faces
forward. Accelerate.

steps.title: 01 The idea — The idea in one picture
steps.note:
The idea:
- We keep the ball to move the opponent, not to keep it. Staggered support all over the pitch gives the man on the ball a short pass, a forward pass and a switch.
- We draw their block towards the ball, find the player they leave free in the centre or a half-space, and once he faces forward we attack at speed.

Roles:
- 2+2 box: centre-backs split, the two deep-lying playmakers close in front of them.
- Fullbacks deep and wide: they feed the inverted wingers.
- Inverted wingers deep in the half-spaces. The 10 in the right half-space beside the RW. The 9 on the blind side of a centre-back.

Coaching points:
- Look at the lines: every pass has an angle, nobody hides behind a teammate.

items.text:
1 · DRAW
We circulate; their
block comes to the ball.
Their CM steps out onto
our DLP.

steps.title: 01 The idea — 1 · Draw them in
steps.note:
Why:
Every player who steps towards the ball leaves space behind him. We want that space, not the ball at his feet.

What happens:
The left centre-back plays out to the left-back. Their wide midfielder jumps the left-back, their striker screens our deep-lying playmaker and their central midfielder steps out of his line to press him. The block has come to the ball.

Coaching points:
- Patience: circulate until a player leaves his zone. The pass that draws is as important as the pass that breaks.
- Our DLP shows to the ball so their midfielder has to choose: follow him, or leave him free.

items.text:
2 · FIND
LB plays the inverted LW
in the space their CM
left. He faces forward.

steps.title: 01 The idea — 2 · Find the free man
steps.note:
What happens:
Their central midfielder has left the left half-space. Our inverted left winger moves into it, and the left-back plays the diagonal into him. He receives on the half-turn, already facing forward. Their other central midfielder slides across to cover, but our 10 and RDM hold him in the centre: he is 8 m away.

Coaching points:
- The free man moves late, into the space as it opens, not before.
- The pass goes into his far foot, so his first touch takes him forward.
- Free in the centre or a half-space is worth more than free on the touchline.

items.text: A
B
C

3 · ACCELERATE
A in behind · B combine
· C wide support. Within
two passes.

steps.title: 01 The idea — 3 · Accelerate: three ways
steps.note:
What happens:
The free man faces forward. Now we go, within two passes or three seconds, before their block recovers.

Coaching points:
- A · Forward pass: the 9 leaves the blind side of the centre-back and attacks the channel behind their fullback.
- B · Combination: the 10 comes inside from the right half-space for a one-two or a set and go.
- C · Wide support: the left-back runs past on the outside and receives in space.
- The first look is forward and in behind (A). If it is closed, combine (B). If both are closed, use the width (C).

Non-negotiable:
Facing forward and free means forward. A pass back from here needs a reason.

items.text:
NO FREE MAN? RECYCLE
Back through the DLPs,
change sides, go again
on the right.

steps.title: 01 The idea — 4 · Nobody free: recycle and go again
steps.note:
What happens:
This time the left side is closed: the space behind their midfielder is covered. We do not force it. The left-back plays back to the left centre-back, who finds the free deep-lying playmaker on the right, who opens the right side.

Coaching points:
- Recycling is part of the plan, not a failure: the block has to shift again, and every shift opens something.
- The DLPs are the hinge: through them we change sides in two passes.
- Change sides quickly: the faster the switch, the bigger the gap on the far side.

Link to the game model:
Our main progression is on the right (patterns P4 and P5), so a recycle to the right is a good outcome.

items.text:
DRAW
circulate · they come to the ball

FIND
the free man in the centre
or a half-space

FACE FORWARD
he receives on the half-turn

ACCELERATE
in behind · combine · wide

NO FREE MAN
recycle and
go again

steps.title: 01 The idea — The cycle
steps.note:
The idea:
- Every possession runs the same cycle: draw, find, face forward, accelerate. When the find does not come, we recycle and draw again.
- Players should be able to say which part of the cycle they are in at any moment.

Questions to ask:
- Who are we drawing right now?
- Who will be free if their midfielder steps out?
- He faces forward: what is the fastest way to goal?

items.text:
1 · POSSESSION ON PURPOSE
Every pass draws, finds or accelerates.

2 · QUICK FROM DEEP
Third-man combinations beat the first press.

3 · DISRUPT THEIR STRUCTURE
Pull players out of their lines, then play behind them.

4 · OVERLOAD THE CENTRE
More of us than them between the lines.

5 · PROGRESS FROM THE RIGHT
Wide and inside: RB, RDM, RW and the 10.

steps.title: 02 Identity — Who we are
steps.note:
The idea:
- Five ideas describe how we want to look with the ball. Every pattern and every session in this model serves at least one of them.

Coaching points:
- Possession on purpose: the ball moves to move them.
- Quick from deep: we accept pressure near our goal because it opens the pitch.
- Disrupt: a player out of his line is a hole in their structure.
- Overload the centre: the shortest way to goal is through the middle.
- Progress from the right: our best combinations live there, so we feed them most.

items.text: DRAWS
FINDS
ACCELERATES

POSSESSION ON PURPOSE
Every pass draws, finds
or accelerates.

steps.title: 02 Identity — 1 · Possession on purpose
steps.note:
The idea:
- We do not count passes, we count purposes. A pass that does none of the three jobs is a wasted pass.

Coaching points:
- Draws: it pulls an opponent out of his position.
- Finds: it reaches the free man, ideally facing forward.
- Accelerates: it takes us forward, past a line, at speed.
- If a pass cannot do any of them, keep the ball and move it to where one of them is possible.

Questions to ask:
- What was that pass for?

items.text:
QUICK FROM DEEP
GK → DLP → bounce to the
LCB → the inverted LW.

steps.title: 02 Identity — 2 · Quick combinations from deep
steps.note:
The idea:
- When they press high we stay calm and use the third man: the goalkeeper finds a deep-lying playmaker, who bounces first time on an angle to the centre-back their striker left. Three passes and we are past two lines.

Coaching points:
- The DLP never turns with a man on his back: one touch, on an angle.
- The third man (here the LCB) receives facing forward and plays forward at once.
- Our inverted winger comes deep into the space their midfielder left.

Link to the game model:
Pattern P1 builds this step by step.

items.text: HE LEFT THIS
HE LEFT THIS

DISRUPT
Pull players out of
their lines, then play
into the space they
leave.

steps.title: 02 Identity — 3 · Disrupt their structure
steps.note:
The idea:
- A block is strong while every player stays in his line. Our movement asks them to leave it: their central midfielder follows our DLP, their fullback follows our inverted winger.
- Each time one of them leaves his line, a space opens behind him. We play into that space at once.

Coaching points:
- Move to drag, not only to receive.
- Read the jump: the player who left is the arrow to the space.
- The space behind a jumping player lasts two or three seconds. Play early.

items.text: BETWEEN THE LINES

OVERLOAD THE CENTRE
Five of ours against
their two central
midfielders.

steps.title: 02 Identity — 4 · Overload the centre
steps.note:
The idea:
- Their midfield has two central players. Between and in front of their lines we have five: the two DLPs, both inverted wingers and the 10. The 9 pins their centre-backs from a blind side.
- Five against two in the middle means someone is always free. Our job is to find him with the right timing.

Coaching points:
- Inverted wingers and the 10 stay between the lines, in different lanes and at different heights.
- The DLPs feed them from behind the strikers.
- Wide areas are for the fullbacks, and for the 10 when the right wing empties.

items.text:
PROGRESS FROM THE RIGHT
Wide and inside: RB,
RDM, RW and the 10.

steps.title: 02 Identity — 5 · Progress from the right
steps.note:
The idea:
- Our right side is the engine: the right-back deep and wide, the right DLP beside him, the inverted right winger and the 10 in the same half-space.
- From there we progress wide (the 10 into the empty wing when their fullback follows our winger) and inside (the 10 dropping to receive, then driving).

Coaching points:
- The RB, RDM, RW and the 10 rotate: one deep, one wide, one inside, one between the lines.
- When the right is closed we have already drawn them: switch to the left.

Link to the game model:
Patterns P4, P5 and P7.

items.text:
4-2-3-1 ON PAPER
The shape we defend in
and leave from.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — On paper: 4-2-3-1
steps.note:
The idea:
- Our starting shape is a 4-2-3-1: a back four, two holding midfielders, the 10 behind the 9 with a winger each side.
- It is the shape we defend in, and the shape we leave from when we win the ball. With the ball, every player moves to a job, shown on the next slide.

Roles:
- GK 1 · RB 2 · LB 3 · RCB 4 · LCB 5 · LDM 6 · RW 7 · RDM 8 · 9 · 10 · LW 11.

items.text:
WITH THE BALL
Everyone moves to his
job.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — With the ball: everyone to his job
steps.note:
What happens:
The centre-backs split, the two DMs stay close in front of them, the fullbacks hold deep and wide, the wingers come inside and deep into the half-spaces, the 10 moves into the right half-space beside the RW, and the 9 leaves the middle for the blind side of a centre-back.

Coaching points:
- Every move has a reason: to give an angle, to drag a man, or to pin a defender.
- The shape is flexible: the jobs stay, the players may swap them (the 10 and the RW, the RB and the RDM).

items.text:
IN POSSESSION
2+2 box, deep fullbacks,
inverted wingers, 10
right, 9 on a blind
side.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — Our shape in possession
steps.note:
Roles:
- 2+2 box: LCB, RCB, LDM, RDM. The DMs are deep-lying playmakers 8 to 10 m in front of the centre-backs.
- Fullbacks deep and wide, level with or just ahead of the DLPs.
- Inverted wingers in the half-spaces, between or just in front of their midfield line.
- The 10 in the right half-space, a few metres from the RW, never in the centre.
- The 9 on the blind side of a centre-back: outside and behind his shoulder, never between the two.

Coaching points:
- From above it looks like a 2-2 with two wide outlets, four players in front and a 9 on a shoulder.

items.text: LEFT WING
LEFT HALF-SPACE
CENTRE
RIGHT HALF-SPACE
RIGHT WING

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — The five channels
steps.note:
The idea:
- We talk about five channels running the length of the pitch: the two wings, the two half-spaces and the centre.

Roles:
- Wings: the fullbacks, deep. The 10 when the right wing empties. The LB when he overlaps.
- Half-spaces: the inverted wingers; on the right also the 10.
- Centre: the DLPs in the first phase; nobody parks there between the lines, players arrive into it.
- The 9 moves between the centre and a half-space, always on a centre-back’s blind side.

Coaching points:
- Two players in the same channel must be at different heights.
- The half-spaces are where we want to receive facing forward: they open angles to the goal and to both sides.

items.text:
GK AND CENTRE-BACKS
Bait the press, split
wide, carry when free.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — Goalkeeper and centre-backs
steps.note:
Roles:
- Goalkeeper: the first playmaker and the bait. He stops the ball, invites the press, then plays into the space it leaves.
- Centre-backs: split to the width of the box, so the goalkeeper and the DLPs can play between them.
- A centre-back who receives facing forward carries the ball into midfield until a player comes out to him.

Coaching points:
- Bait: hold the ball until a presser commits, then play past him.
- Centre-backs receive side-on, already facing the pitch.
- Their first look is forward: the inverted winger in the half-space, then the 9 on the blind side.

items.text:
THE DLPs
Close to the CBs. Slide
to your fullback for the
diagonal.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — The DLPs: deep-lying playmakers
steps.note:
Roles:
- The two DMs stay within about 10 m of the centre-backs while we build, forming the 2+2 box. The rings show that distance.
- Each DLP slides towards his own fullback when the ball goes wide, to offer the diagonal pass inside.
- They switch play: through them we change sides in two passes.

Coaching points:
- Close enough to the centre-backs for a short pass under pressure; far enough apart that one striker cannot screen both.
- A man on your back: bounce first time on an angle to a centre-back or the other DLP. Free: turn and play forward.
- Never both DLPs in the same lane or at the same height.

Non-negotiable:
The DLPs are close to the centre-backs until the ball is past their first line.

items.text:
FULLBACKS
Deep and wide. The
diagonal into the
inverted winger.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — Fullbacks: deep and wide
steps.note:
Roles:
- The fullbacks hold the width, deep, level with or just ahead of the DLPs. They pin the opposition wide midfielders and give the centre-backs an outlet.
- Their key pass is the diagonal inside to the inverted winger in the half-space. Their second is the diagonal back to the DLP.
- In the final third they arrive as wide support, late, when the winger and the 10 have taken their defenders inside (pattern P7).

Coaching points:
- On the touchline, side-on, already facing the half-space.
- Play the inverted winger the moment their central midfielder leaves his zone.
- Do not push high early: deep fullbacks keep the opponent’s wide players honest and protect us on the counter.

items.text:
INVERTED WINGERS
Deep in the half-spaces.
Receive from the
fullback, facing
forward.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — Inverted wingers: deep in the half-spaces
steps.note:
Roles:
- The wingers start inside and deep, in the half-spaces, between or just in front of the opposition midfield line.
- They receive the diagonal from the deep fullback, on the half-turn, facing forward, in the space our DLP has dragged their midfielder out of.
- When their fullback follows them inside, they set first time on an angle and the space behind that fullback is ours (the 9 on the left, the 10 on the right).

Coaching points:
- Arrive in the space as it opens, not before.
- Scan before the ball arrives: is their fullback following?
- Free: turn and accelerate. A man on your back: set first time on an angle.

Non-negotiable:
The winger never stands on the touchline in our build-up: the touchline belongs to the fullback.

items.text: A
B

THE 10
A into the empty wing ·
B drop, drive, sprint
from deep.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — The 10: right half-space, two jobs
steps.note:
Roles:
- The 10 lives in the right half-space, a few metres from the RW, never in the centre.
- A · Their fullback follows our RW inside: the right wing is empty, and the 10 slides into it (pattern P4).
- B · Nobody follows: he drops deep to receive facing forward, drives at their midfield, then sprints from deep into the box (pattern P5).

Coaching points:
- Watch their fullback: his decision chooses your job.
- Arrive late in the box, from deep: late runners are hard to mark.

Non-negotiable:
The 10 does not occupy the centre. He arrives into it.

items.text: NOT HERE

THE 9
On a blind side. Attack
the channel their
fullback leaves.

steps.title: 03 Shape and roles — The 9: blind side, never between
steps.note:
Roles:
- The 9 stands on the blind side of a centre-back: outside and slightly behind his shoulder, where the centre-back cannot see him and the ball at the same time.
- Never between the two centre-backs: there both can mark him and neither has to turn.
- When their fullback follows our inverted winger inside, the channel behind that fullback opens. The 9 attacks it.

Coaching points:
- Move as the ball moves: always on the blind side of the centre-back nearest the ball.
- Make the centre-back turn his head. Every look at you is a look away from the ball.
- Run from the blind side into the channel, timed with the pass, never early.

Non-negotiable:
The 9 is never between the centre-backs.

items.text:
1 · STAGGER: no two players in the same lane or line
2 · THE 2+2 BOX: DLPs close to the centre-backs
3 · BODIES: a man on your back, set on an angle
4 · PURPOSE: every pass draws, finds or accelerates
5 · FREE AND FACING FORWARD: we accelerate
6 · PIN AND THREATEN: the 9 on a blind side
7 · REST DEFENCE 2+2 and a 5-second counter-press
8 · THE RIGHT IS OUR ENGINE: one deep, one wide, one inside

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — The eight non-negotiables
steps.note:
The idea:
- These are the rules we never break, whatever the opponent does. Patterns change week to week; these do not.

Coaching points:
- Coach them by name: “Stagger!”, “Box!”, “Set!”, “Purpose!”, “Go!”, “Blind side!”, “Rest!”, “Engine!”.

items.text:
1 · STAGGER
Triangles and diamonds,
never flat lines.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 1 · Stagger
steps.note:
Why:
Staggered players form triangles and diamonds. Every player on the ball then has a pass forward, a pass sideways and a pass back, each on a different angle, and one presser cannot cover two of them.

Coaching points:
- Check the player in front: if you can see him straight through, move a step sideways.
- Height and lane: different from the teammate nearest you in both.

Non-negotiable:
No two players in the same lane at the same height, and no three in a flat line.

items.text:
2 · THE 2+2 BOX
DLPs within 10 m of the
centre-backs.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 2 · The 2+2 box
steps.note:
Why:
Against a press the box gives the goalkeeper and centre-backs two short, central options, and every pass into a DLP has a third man behind it. Far from the centre-backs, a DLP is a long, risky pass.

Coaching points:
- Open your body to the goalkeeper and the far side at once.
- If their striker screens you, move one step to leave his shadow.

Non-negotiable:
Until the ball is past their first line, the two DLPs stay within about 10 m of the centre-backs.

items.text:
A MAN ON YOUR BACK
set first time, on an angle

FREE AND SIDE-ON
play forward

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 3 · Bodies
steps.note:
Why:
Turning into a man on your back loses the ball in the worst place. A first-time set on an angle (a V, or a zigzag of passes) is quicker than any defender and finds a teammate who can see the pitch.

Coaching points:
- Scan before the ball arrives: who is behind me?
- Receive half-turned, side-on, so you can see the passer and the pitch.
- Set with the foot away from the defender.

Non-negotiable:
A player with a man on his back never turns. He sets it first time, on an angle, to a teammate facing forward. Only a free, side-on player plays the ball on in the direction it came.

items.text: DRAWS
FINDS

4 · PURPOSE
Draw, find or
accelerate. Otherwise
recycle and switch.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 4 · Purpose
steps.note:
Why:
Possession without a purpose lets the opponent rest in his shape. Possession with a purpose moves him until a gap appears.

Coaching points:
- Before you pass, know its job.
- A sideways pass is good if it draws; a forward pass is bad if it only gives the ball away.

Non-negotiable:
Every pass draws, finds or accelerates. If none is possible, we recycle through the DLPs and switch, never force.

items.text:
TWO PASSES OR
THREE SECONDS

5 · GO
Free and facing forward:
the next action is
forward.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 5 · Free and facing forward: go
steps.note:
Why:
Their block recovers in about three seconds. Facing forward in a half-space is the moment the whole cycle was built for.

Coaching points:
- Everyone in front of the ball moves the moment he faces forward: the 9 in behind, the 10 inside, the far winger to the far post.
- Players behind the ball push up to support and protect.

Non-negotiable:
When a player receives free and facing forward, the next action goes forward: a pass in behind, a carry into space, or a combination. Within two passes or three seconds.

items.text: NOT HERE

6 · PIN AND THREATEN
Blind side. Attack the
channel the fullback
leaves.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 6 · Pin and threaten
steps.note:
Why:
A 9 between the centre-backs is easy to mark. On a blind side he pins a centre-back and is one run from the channel a jumping fullback leaves.

Coaching points:
- Their fullback steps in: go, timed with the pass.
- If the run is not found, return to the blind side at once.

Non-negotiable:
The 9 is always on the blind side of a centre-back, never between them. Whenever their fullback follows one of our inverted wingers, someone attacks the channel behind him: the 9 on the left, the 10 on the right.

items.text:
7 · REST DEFENCE
Two CBs, one DLP, the
far fullback. Press 5
seconds.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 7 · Rest defence and the counter-press
steps.note:
Why:
We attack with many players inside, so we lose the ball inside too. The rest defence stops the counter; the counter-press wins the ball back near their goal.

Coaching points:
- The DLP who stays sits in front of the centre-backs, in the centre.
- The far fullback tucks in level with the centre-backs.
- Lose it: the nearest three close the ball, the rest close the passing lanes.

Non-negotiable:
While we attack, four stay behind the ball: both centre-backs, one DLP and the far-side fullback. When we lose it, the nearest three press the ball for 5 seconds.

items.text:
8 · THE ENGINE
Deep, wide, inside,
between the lines. Swap
jobs, never leave one.

steps.title: 04 Non-negotiables — 8 · The right is our engine
steps.note:
Why:
Our best combinations live on the right. Rotations confuse their markers; four fixed jobs keep our shape.

Coaching points:
- The RW goes inside: the 10 takes the wing or the RB stays wide.
- The 10 drops: the RW pushes up between the lines.
- The RB arrives late as wide support: the RDM holds deep.

Non-negotiable:
On the right, the RB, RDM, RW and 10 always cover four jobs: one deep, one wide, one inside, one between the lines. They may swap jobs, never leave one empty.

items.text:
P1 · THIRD MAN FROM DEEP
GK → DLP → bounce to the
LCB → inverted LW → go.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- The goalkeeper baits their striker, plays into a deep-lying playmaker, who bounces first time to the centre-back the striker left. That centre-back faces forward and finds the inverted winger, who has come deep into the space their midfielder left.
- GK → LDM → LCB (third man) → LW → accelerate.

Roles:
- GK: the bait.
- LDM: the wall, one touch on an angle.
- LCB: the third man, facing forward.
- LW: inverted, deep, into the space.
- The 9: blind side of their right centre-back, ready to attack the channel.

Trigger:
They press high with two strikers on our centre-backs and their central midfielders on our DLPs.

Link to the game model:
Identity 2 (quick from deep) and non-negotiables 2 (the box) and 3 (bodies).

items.text:
1 · BAIT
GK holds. Their striker
jumps and blocks the
LCB.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — 1 · Bait: the goalkeeper holds
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper stops the ball. Their left-sided striker jumps him, curving his run so his shadow blocks the pass to our left centre-back.

Coaching points:
- The pause is a question: hold until a presser commits.
- His curve tells us which pass he closed: the LCB. So the LCB will be the third man.

items.text:
2 · INTO THE DLP
GK plays the LDM. Their
CM jumps his back.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — 2 · Into the DLP: their CM jumps
steps.note:
What happens:
The goalkeeper plays into the left DLP, close in front of the centre-backs. Their central midfielder jumps onto his back as the ball travels.

Coaching points:
- The DLP shows half-turned, open to the left centre-back.
- Goalkeeper: firm, into the foot away from the presser.
- The DLP knows before the ball arrives: a man on my back, so I set.

items.text:
3 · THIRD MAN
The LDM bounces first
time to the LCB, who
faces forward.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — 3 · Bounce to the LCB: the third man
steps.note:
What happens:
The DLP bounces the ball first time, back on an angle, to the left centre-back. The goalkeeper could not reach him; the DLP could. The LCB receives facing forward with nobody near him.

Coaching points:
- One touch, with the foot away from the presser. The shape is a V: in from the goalkeeper, out to the LCB.
- The LCB steps out of the striker’s shadow as the first pass travels.
- Third man: A cannot reach C, so A plays B and B sets C.

Non-negotiable:
The DLP does not turn into the man on his back.

items.text:
4 · INTO THE SPACE
LCB plays the inverted
LW where their CM was.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — 4 · LCB finds the inverted LW
steps.note:
What happens:
Their central midfielder left his zone to press our DLP. Our inverted left winger has come deep into it. The left centre-back, facing forward, plays him: he receives on the half-turn, already facing their goal.

Coaching points:
- The winger arrives as the set is played, not before.
- Pass into his far foot: his first touch goes forward.
- Two lines broken in three passes.

items.text:
5 · ACCELERATE
LW carries; the 9
attacks the channel from
the blind side.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — 5 · Accelerate: carry, then in behind
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger is free and facing forward: he carries the ball at their back line. As their fullback hesitates, the 9 leaves the blind side of their centre-back and runs into the channel; the winger plays him in.

Coaching points:
- Carry until a defender commits, then pass.
- The 9’s run starts as the winger’s head comes up.
- The 10 and the RW arrive in the box behind the play.

If it is not on:
- Their fullback steps out to the winger: the channel is open, play the 9 at once.
- Their centre-back follows the 9: the winger keeps carrying, or finds the 10 inside.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Bait · set on an angle ·
third man forward ·
winger into the space.

steps.title: P1 Build-up · Third man from deep — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Bait: the goalkeeper holds until a presser commits.
- The DLP sets first time on an angle: never turn with a man on your back.
- The third man (the centre-back) faces forward and plays forward at once.
- The inverted winger comes deep into the space, late.
- Facing forward: carry, then in behind.

Questions to ask:
- Which pass did their striker’s curve close?
- Who was free when their midfielder jumped?
- Why did the DLP bounce it instead of turning?

If it is not on:
- Their CM does not jump: the DLP is free; he turns and plays the winger himself.
- Their striker blocks the DLP: goalkeeper to the far centre-back, and the same pattern on the right with the RDM and RCB.

items.text:
P2 · DRAG AND FIND
The DLP drags their CM;
the LB finds the
inverted LW.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- Our left DLP drags their central midfielder out of his line. He bounces first time to the left-back, who plays the diagonal into the inverted left winger in the space the midfielder left. The winger faces forward and we accelerate.
- LCB → LDM → LB → LW → carry → 9 in behind → cutback.

Trigger:
They defend in a 4-4-2 mid-block. Our left centre-back has the ball.

Link to the game model:
The idea, slides 1-3. Identity 3 (disrupt).

items.text:
1 · DRAG
LCB plays the DLP. Their
CM steps out onto him.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — 1 · The DLP drags their midfielder
steps.note:
What happens:
The left DLP shows to the ball and the left centre-back plays him. Their central midfielder steps out of his line to press him, onto his back.

Coaching points:
- The DLP shows half-turned, open to the left-back.
- The pass into him is firm: it must pull their midfielder, not give him time to think.
- Our inverted LW watches the midfielder: when he steps out, the space behind him is the target.

items.text:
2 · BOUNCE
The DLP sets first time
to the LB; the LW moves
into the space.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — 2 · Bounce to the left-back
steps.note:
What happens:
The DLP has a man on his back: he bounces first time on an angle to the left-back. As the ball travels, their wide midfielder jumps the left-back and our winger moves into the space their midfielder left.

Coaching points:
- A V: in from the LCB, out to the LB. The DLP never turns.
- The left-back receives side-on, already facing the half-space.
- The winger arrives late: as the bounce is played.

items.text:
3 · FIND
LB plays the diagonal
into the inverted LW. He
faces forward.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — 3 · The diagonal into the inverted winger
steps.note:
What happens:
The left-back plays the diagonal inside into the inverted winger. He receives on the half-turn, facing forward: the midfielder who stepped out is behind him, their other central midfielder is 8 m away, held in the centre by our 10 and RDM, and their fullback has not moved.

Coaching points:
- The diagonal is played on the ground, firm, into the far foot.
- The winger’s first touch goes forward, towards the back line.

Non-negotiable:
Free and facing forward: go (non-negotiable 5).

items.text:
4 · ACCELERATE
LW carries; their FB
narrows; the 9 runs into
the channel.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — 4 · Carry and slip the 9
steps.note:
What happens:
The winger carries the ball at their back line. Their fullback narrows to stop him; the 9 leaves the blind side of their centre-back and runs into the channel the fullback has left. The winger slips him in.

Coaching points:
- Carry at a defender to make him decide.
- The 9 runs on the blind side, outside the centre-back, timed with the winger’s head coming up.
- Weight the pass into his path, not his feet.

items.text:
5 · CUTBACK
LW near post, 10 penalty
spot, RW far post.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — 5 · Cutback and arrivals
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 drives to the byline and cuts back behind their centre-backs, who are running towards their own goal. The LW attacks the near post, the 10 arrives at the penalty spot from the right half-space, the RW attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- Cutback along the ground, behind the defenders running back.
- Three runners, three lanes: near post, penalty spot, far post.
- Finish first time.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Drag · bounce · diagonal
· face forward · go.

steps.title: P2 Left · Drag and find — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The DLP drags: show, receive, bounce first time on an angle.
- The left-back receives side-on and plays the diagonal at once.
- The winger arrives into the space late and receives facing forward.
- Accelerate within two passes: carry, then in behind.
- Arrivals: near post, penalty spot, far post.

Questions to ask:
- When did the space behind their midfielder open?
- Why did the winger wait before moving into it?

If it is not on:
- Their midfielder does not step out: the DLP turns and plays the winger himself.
- Their fullback follows the winger: pattern P3.

items.text:
P3 · THEIR FB FOLLOWS
The LW takes him away;
the 9 attacks the
channel he left.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- We use it. The winger drops and takes the fullback with him. The left-back plays into the winger, who sets first time on an angle to the left DLP. The DLP, facing forward, plays the 9 into the channel the fullback left.
- LCB → LB → LW (set) → LDM → 9 in behind.

Trigger:
Their right fullback follows our inverted left winger inside whenever he drops.

Link to the game model:
Non-negotiable 6: pin and threaten.

items.text:
1 · TAKE HIM AWAY
The LW drops; their
fullback follows him.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — 1 · The winger drops; their fullback follows
steps.note:
What happens:
The left centre-back plays out to the left-back. Our inverted winger drops towards the ball and their fullback follows him, tight. Our left DLP slides towards the left-back to offer the diagonal.

Coaching points:
- The winger drops slowly at first: let the fullback commit.
- The DLP slides to the left-back’s side: close, diagonal, inside him.
- The 9 watches the fullback, not the ball.

items.text:
2 · SET
LB into the LW, who sets
first time to the DLP.
The 9 goes.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — 2 · Into the winger, set to the DLP
steps.note:
What happens:
The left-back plays into the winger. With the fullback on his back he does not turn: he sets first time, back on an angle, to the DLP, who faces forward. As the set travels, the 9 leaves the blind side and runs into the channel.

Coaching points:
- A V: in from the left-back, out to the DLP.
- The winger sets with the foot away from the fullback, then spins.
- The 9 runs as the set is played, outside the centre-back, into the space behind the fullback.

Non-negotiable:
A man on your back: set first time on an angle.

items.text:
3 · IN BEHIND
The DLP, facing forward,
finds the 9 in the
channel.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — 3 · The DLP plays the 9 in behind
steps.note:
What happens:
The DLP, facing forward, plays the ball into the channel the fullback left, driven or lofted, into the 9’s path. The winger spins in behind too, and the 10 and RW head for the box.

Coaching points:
- Into space, ahead of the runner, not to his feet.
- Driven on the ground if the lane is clear; lofted over the fullback if not.
- The winger spins after his set: two runners in the channel.

items.text:
4 · FINISH
9 cuts back; 10 arrives
at the penalty spot.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — 4 · Finish
steps.note:
What happens:
The 9 drives at goal from the channel and cuts back to the 10 arriving at the penalty spot. The LW attacks the near post, the RW the far post.

Coaching points:
- If the angle is open, shoot. If not, cut back behind the defenders.
- Late arrivals win cutbacks.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Take him away · set on
an angle · 9 into the
channel.

steps.title: P3 Left · Their FB follows: 9 in behind — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The winger drops to take the fullback away, slowly, then sets first time on an angle.
- The DLP slides to the left-back’s side to receive the set facing forward.
- The 9 attacks the channel from the blind side, timed with the set.
- Pass into space, ahead of the runner.

Questions to ask:
- Who followed our winger? What did he leave behind?
- When does the 9 start his run?

If it is not on:
- Their centre-back slides across with the 9: the space between the centre-backs opens, the 10 arrives into it.
- Their fullback does not follow: pattern P2, the winger receives facing forward.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- The right side empties: their wide midfielder has jumped our right-back and their fullback has gone inside with our winger. The 10 slides from the right half-space into the empty wing and receives facing forward.
- RCB → RB → RW (set) → RDM → 10 in the empty wing → cutback.

Roles:
- The 9 has moved to the blind side of their left centre-back, on the ball side.

Trigger:
Their left fullback follows our inverted right winger inside.

Link to the game model:
Identity 5 (progress from the right) and the 10’s job A.

items.text:
1 · OUT
RCB to RB. Their wide
midfielder jumps him.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — 1 · Out to the right-back
steps.note:
What happens:
The right centre-back plays out to the right-back. Their wide midfielder jumps him. Our right DLP slides across, inside the right-back, to offer the diagonal.

Coaching points:
- Right-back: side-on on the touchline, facing the half-space.
- RDM: close and diagonal, inside the right-back.

items.text:
2 · TAKE HIM AWAY
The RW drops; their
fullback follows him.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — 2 · Into the RW: their fullback follows
steps.note:
What happens:
Our inverted right winger drops inside and their left fullback follows him, tight. The right-back plays into the winger.

Coaching points:
- The winger drops to pull the fullback, not to turn.
- The 10 watches the fullback: when he goes inside, the wing is empty.

items.text:
3 · SET AND SLIDE
RW sets to the DLP; the
10 slides into the empty
wing.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — 3 · Set to the DLP; the 10 takes the wing
steps.note:
What happens:
With the fullback on his back the winger sets first time, back on an angle, to the right DLP. As the set travels, the 10 slides from the right half-space into the empty wing.

Coaching points:
- A V: in from the right-back, out to the DLP.
- The 10 moves as the set is played: into the space behind their wide midfielder, ahead of where their fullback was.

Non-negotiable:
The right is our engine: one deep (RDM), one wide (the 10 now), one inside (RW), the RB behind.

items.text:
4 · FIND THE 10
The DLP plays the 10 in
the empty wing.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — 4 · The DLP finds the 10 facing forward
steps.note:
What happens:
The DLP, facing forward, plays the 10 in the empty wing. The 10 receives on the run, facing forward, 15 m from the nearest defender.

Coaching points:
- Pass into the 10’s path, on the ground.
- The 10 attacks the space at once, towards the byline.
- The 9 holds the blind side of their left centre-back; the RW spins towards the box.

items.text:
5 · CUT BACK
9 near post, RW penalty
spot, LW far post.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — 5 · Drive and cut back
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 drives to the byline and cuts back. The 9 attacks the near post from the blind side, the RW arrives at the penalty spot, the LW attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- The 10 runs at the byline, not inside: inside is where their defenders are.
- Cut back behind the defenders running towards their goal.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Draw two · set on an
angle · the 10 into the
empty wing.

steps.title: P4 Right · 10 into the empty wing — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The RB draws their wide midfielder; the RW draws their fullback.
- The RW sets first time on an angle to the DLP.
- The 10 reads their fullback and slides into the empty wing as the set is played.
- The DLP plays the 10 facing forward, into his path.

Questions to ask:
- Who left the right wing? When did you know it was empty?

If it is not on:
- Their fullback does not follow the RW: the RW receives facing forward and combines with the 10 (one-two inside).
- Their wide midfielder tracks the 10: the RB is free, play him (pattern P7).

items.text:
P5 · DROP, DRIVE, SPRINT
The 10 receives deep,
drives, plays the 9,
arrives late.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- The 10 drops deep in the right half-space and receives facing forward. He drives at their midfield, plays the 9 into the right channel, then sprints from deep into the box for the cutback.
- RW and 10 swap heights: when the 10 drops, the RW pushes up between the lines.

Trigger:
Their fullback stays at home and their midfield does not follow our 10 when he drops.

Link to the game model:
The 10’s job B. Non-negotiable 8: the engine.

items.text:
1 · DROP
The 10 drops; the RW
pushes up and out.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — 1 · The 10 drops, the RW pushes up
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 drops into the right half-space, in front of their midfield line. Nobody follows him. The RW pushes up and out between the lines to keep their fullback busy.

Coaching points:
- Drop on the half-turn, already seeing the pitch.
- The RW and the 10 swap heights, never both deep.

items.text:
2 · RECEIVE
RCB plays the 10; he
faces forward.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — 2 · RCB to the 10
steps.note:
What happens:
The right centre-back plays into the 10, who receives on the half-turn, already facing forward. Their nearest striker is 6 m away, behind him; their midfielders hold their line.

Coaching points:
- Receive across the body, first touch forward.
- Free and side-on: play forward (non-negotiable 3).

items.text:
3 · DRIVE
The 10 drives; the 9
runs into the channel.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — 3 · Drive, then the 9 into the channel
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 drives at the gap between their central and wide midfielders. Their central midfielder steps to him. The 9 leaves the blind side of their left centre-back and runs into the channel; the 10 slips him in.

Coaching points:
- Drive until someone steps out to you, then pass.
- The 9 runs outside the centre-back, inside the fullback.
- The 10 does not stop after the pass: he sprints.

items.text:
4 · SPRINT FROM DEEP
The 10 arrives late for
the cutback.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — 4 · Sprint from deep
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10 sprints from deep into the box. The 9 drives at the byline and cuts back to him at the penalty spot. The LW attacks the far post, the RW the edge of the box.

Coaching points:
- Late runs from deep are the hardest to track: their midfielders are facing their own goal.
- Arrive at the penalty spot as the cutback is played, not before.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Drop · face forward ·
drive · pass · sprint.

steps.title: P5 Right · The 10 drops, drives, sprints — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The 10 drops only when nobody follows him; the RW pushes up as he drops.
- Receive facing forward, then drive at a gap.
- Pass when a defender steps out, then sprint.
- The 9 attacks the channel from the blind side.

Questions to ask:
- Did anyone follow you when you dropped?
- When did their midfielder step out?

If it is not on:
- Their midfielder follows the 10 down: the RW is free between the lines; the RCB plays him.
- Their fullback follows the RW up: pattern P4, the 10 into the empty wing.

items.text:
P6 · UP, BACK, THROUGH
The 9 comes short, sets
to the 10, the LW goes
in behind.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- Our left DLP drags their central midfielder out of his line. The 9 comes short from the blind side into the left half-space, between their lines, and the left centre-back plays into him. He sets first time on an angle to the 10, who arrives from the right half-space into the hole the dragged midfielder left. The 10, facing forward, plays the LW in behind.
- Up (LCB → 9), back (9 → 10), through (10 → LW).

Trigger:
Their centre-backs follow our 9 when he comes short.

Link to the game model:
Identity 4 (overload the centre).

items.text:
1 · UP
The DLP drags their CM;
the 9 comes short. LCB
plays him.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — 1 · Up: into the 9
steps.note:
What happens:
Our left DLP shows to the ball and drags their central midfielder out of his line. That opens the lane: the 9 checks short from the blind side into the space between their lines, their centre-back follows him, and the left centre-back plays straight into the 9’s feet.

Coaching points:
- The 9 comes short when the centre-back’s head is turned, and protects the ball with his body.
- A firm pass on the ground into the foot away from the defender.

items.text:
2 · BACK
The 9 sets first time to
the 10, arriving in the
hole their CM left.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — 2 · Back: set to the 10
steps.note:
What happens:
With their centre-back on his back, the 9 sets first time on an angle to the 10, who arrives from the right half-space into the hole their dragged midfielder left, facing forward. Their other central midfielder is still guarding the centre. The LW starts his run in behind as the set travels.

Coaching points:
- A V: up from the LCB, back to the 10.
- The 10 arrives into the hole the dragged midfielder left; he never waits in the centre.
- The LW runs inside their fullback, into the space behind their centre-back.

items.text:
3 · THROUGH
The 10 plays the LW in
behind.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — 3 · Through: the LW in behind
steps.note:
What happens:
The 10, facing forward, plays the LW in behind their back line. The 9 spins off his centre-back, round the outside, then attacks the near post; the RW attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- Through ball into the runner’s path, behind the centre-back who stepped out.
- The 9 spins the moment he has set the ball.

items.text:
4 · FINISH
Shoot across the
goalkeeper, or cut back.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — 4 · Shoot or cut back
steps.note:
What happens:
The LW drives into the box and shoots across the goalkeeper, or cuts back to the 9 or the RW.

Coaching points:
- Shoot early when the angle is open.
- If the goalkeeper comes, square it.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Up from the CB · back to
the 10 · through to the
LW.

steps.title: P6 Centre · Up, back, through — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The 9 comes short from a blind side, never from between the centre-backs.
- He sets first time on an angle, then spins.
- The 10 arrives into the centre facing forward.
- The LW runs in behind as the set is played.

Questions to ask:
- Who followed the 9? What did he leave?
- Why does the 10 arrive instead of waiting in the centre?

If it is not on:
- Their centre-back does not follow the 9: the 9 turns and drives.
- Their midfielder blocks the 10: the 9 sets to the LDM, who switches to the right.

items.text:
P7 · THE RIGHT-BACK ARRIVES
Inside players drag the
defenders; the RB
arrives outside.

steps.title: P7 Wide support · The right-back arrives — Set-up
steps.note:
The idea:
- The RW receives inside and drives across their fullback. With the 10 inside too, the right wing is empty: the right-back arrives late, outside, and the RW plays him. Low cross or cutback.
- RB → RW → carry inside → RB overlaps → cutback.

Roles:
- The RDM holds deep while the RB goes: the engine keeps one player deep.

Trigger:
The RW and the 10 have taken their defenders inside.

Link to the game model:
The idea: accelerate with wide support. Non-negotiable 8.

items.text:
1 · INTO THE RW
RB plays the inverted
RW, who faces forward.

steps.title: P7 Wide support · The right-back arrives — 1 · RB into the RW
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back plays the diagonal into the inverted right winger, who receives on the half-turn, facing forward. Their nearest midfielder is 7 m away, their fullback 22 m.

Coaching points:
- Free and side-on: turn and face their back line.
- The right-back follows his pass: the run starts now.

items.text:
2 · OVERLAP
RW carries inside; the
RB overlaps outside.

steps.title: P7 Wide support · The right-back arrives — 2 · Carry inside, the RB overlaps
steps.note:
What happens:
The RW carries inside at their fullback, who steps in to stop him. The right-back overlaps outside into the space the fullback left, and the RW plays him.

Coaching points:
- Carry inside to drag the fullback, not to shoot.
- The overlap is late and at full speed.
- The 10 holds the inside lane, so the fullback cannot drop back outside.

Non-negotiable:
The RDM holds deep: one stays behind (the engine).

items.text:
3 · CUT BACK
9 near post, 10 penalty
spot, LW far post.

steps.title: P7 Wide support · The right-back arrives — 3 · Low cross or cutback
steps.note:
What happens:
The right-back drives to the byline and cuts back. The 9 attacks the near post, the 10 arrives at the penalty spot, the LW attacks the far post.

Coaching points:
- Low and hard across the six-yard box if the near post is free; cutback if the defenders are running back.

items.text:
COACHING POINTS
Drag inside · arrive
outside · one stays
deep.

steps.title: P7 Wide support · The right-back arrives — Coaching points
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Inside players drag the defenders: the RW carries inside, the 10 holds the inside lane.
- The right-back arrives late and at speed.
- The RDM stays deep while the RB goes.

Questions to ask:
- Who was left to defend the wing when their fullback stepped inside?

If it is not on:
- Their wide midfielder tracks the RB: the RW keeps carrying, or plays the 10 inside.

items.text:
MD-4 · BUILD AND BOX
T1 Box rondo 15 min · T2 Find the inverted winger 25 min

MD-3 · PATTERNS AND PHASE
T3 Pattern runs 20 min · T4 Progress from the right 30 min

MD-2 · THE GAME
T1 short 10 min · T5 Possession on purpose 2 x 12 min

MD-1 · SHARP AND CLEAR
T1 short 8 min · walk-through of P1-P7 15 min

steps.title: 06 Training — The week
steps.note:
The idea:
- Each session teaches part of the model. Early in the week small spaces and many repetitions; later bigger spaces, the whole team, and the game.
- Every session is built around the same cycle: draw, find, face forward, accelerate.

Organisation:
- MD-4: the 2+2 box and the third man (T1), then finding the inverted wingers (T2).
- MD-3: the patterns unopposed and semi-opposed (T3), then a phase of play on the right (T4).
- MD-2: an 11 v 11 game with bonuses for our identity (T5).
- MD-1: a short rondo and a walk-through of the patterns the opponent invites.

Coaching points:
- Name the cycle in every session: “Draw!”, “Find!”, “Face!”, “Go!”.

items.text:
T1 · BOX RONDO
5 v 3. Find a
target through a
gate.

steps.title: T1 Box rondo · 5 v 3 + 2 targets — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 30 x 36 m in front of our goal. Goalkeeper, two centre-backs and two DLPs against three pressers. Two gates on the far line, in the half-space lanes, with the inverted wingers as targets behind them.
- 6 x 2 min, 1 min rest. Rotate the pressers every two bouts.

Rules:
- Blue: two touches. The DLPs stay within 10 m of the centre-backs.
- A pass through a gate to a target scores; the target returns the ball to the goalkeeper.
- Pressers win the ball: they shoot at our goal at once.

Scoring:
- Through a gate: 1 point.
- Through a gate after a first-time set by a DLP (third man): 2 points.
- Pressers: goal 2, winning the ball 1.

Link to the game model:
The 2+2 box (non-negotiable 2) and P1, third man from deep.

items.text:
THIRD MAN · 2
GK → DLP → bounce
to the CB →
through the gate.

steps.title: T1 Box rondo · 5 v 3 + 2 targets — Third man: 2 points
steps.note:
What happens:
A presser jumps the goalkeeper and the third presser jumps the DLP. The goalkeeper plays the DLP, who bounces first time on an angle to the left centre-back, who plays through the gate to the LW: 2 points.

Coaching points:
- The DLP shows half-turned and sets with one touch.
- The centre-back steps out of the presser’s shadow as the first pass travels.
- Through the gate on the ground, into the target’s far foot.

items.text:
FREE DLP · 1
Nobody on his
back: turn and
play the gate.

steps.title: T1 Box rondo · 5 v 3 + 2 targets — Free DLP: turn and play
steps.note:
What happens:
This time the pressers are on the left. The goalkeeper plays the right centre-back, who finds the right DLP free: he receives on the half-turn and plays through the right gate.

Coaching points:
- Scan before receiving: nobody behind me, so I turn.
- Free DLP: one touch to open up, one to pass.

items.text:
PROGRESSIONS
Live targets ·
fullbacks · one
touch.

steps.title: T1 Box rondo · 5 v 3 + 2 targets — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- The box stays a box: 2 + 2, staggered.
- Bait with the goalkeeper; play past the presser who commits.

Progressions:
- Targets become live: a fourth presser marks them, they must set first time back to a DLP or centre-back.
- Add the fullbacks wide and two more pressers: 7 v 5.
- One touch for the DLPs.

Regressions:
- Two pressers only.
- Wider area: 36 x 40 m.

Dose:
6 x 2 min, 1 min rest.

items.text:
T2 · FIND THE INVERTED WINGER
8 v 6. Pockets
and channels.

steps.title: T2 Positional game · Find the inverted winger — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 50 x 60 m. 8 blue (LB, LDM, RDM, RB, LW, RW, 10, 9) against 6 red (four midfielders and two fullbacks).
- Hatched: the half-space pockets. Blue: the channels behind the red fullbacks. Two mini goals on the near line for red.
- 4 x 5 min, 2 min rest.

Rules:
- Blue three touches. The fullbacks stay deep, outside the pockets. The 9 starts on a red fullback’s blind side, never in the middle.
- Red win the ball: they attack the mini goals; blue counter-press for 5 seconds.

Scoring:
- An inverted winger (or the 10) receives in a pocket from a fullback, facing forward: 1 point.
- Then the 9, the 10 or a winger receives in a channel: 2 more points.
- Red: a mini goal 2, a counter-press survived (5 s) 1.

Link to the game model:
The fullbacks feed the inverted wingers (P2); a fullback who follows opens the channel (P3, P4).

items.text:
DRAG AND FIND · 1
The DLP drags,
the LB finds
the LW.

steps.title: T2 Positional game · Find the inverted winger — Drag and find: 1 point
steps.note:
What happens:
The left DLP drags their central midfielder. The left-back receives and plays the diagonal into the inverted left winger in the pocket, facing forward: 1 point.

Coaching points:
- Drag, then find: the pocket opens when their midfielder steps out.
- The winger arrives late and faces forward with his first touch.

items.text:
SET AND IN BEHIND · 2
Their FB
jumps: set,
then the 9 in
the channel.

steps.title: T2 Positional game · Find the inverted winger — Their fullback follows: 2 more
steps.note:
What happens:
Their fullback jumps onto the winger. The winger sets first time back to the left-back, who now faces forward and plays the 9 into the channel the fullback left: 2 more points.

Coaching points:
- Man on your back: set first time on an angle.
- The 9 runs from the blind side as the set is played.

items.text:
PROGRESSIONS
CBs and GK on
· two touches
· the 10 in
the pocket.

steps.title: T2 Positional game · Find the inverted winger — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Fullbacks deep and wide: the pockets are for the wingers.
- Read the jump: whoever leaves his zone opens the space behind him.

Progressions:
- Add two red centre-backs and a goalkeeper; finish on goal after a channel ball.
- Blue two touches.
- The 10 must receive in the right pocket before a goal counts.

Regressions:
- Red fullbacks passive.
- Only 5 red.

Dose:
4 x 5 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
T3 · PATTERN RUNS
Left: LCB → LDM → LB →
LW → 9.

steps.title: T3 Pattern runs · Unopposed to live — Set-up and the left run (P2)
steps.note:
Organisation:
- Full pitch, our whole team, mannequins in their 4-4-2 mid-block. Two groups: one runs the left pattern, the other the right, then swap.
- Stage 1 unopposed at walking pace, stage 2 at match speed, stage 3 with passive players instead of mannequins, stage 4 with live defenders.
- 20 min, 6-8 reps a side per stage.

Rules:
- Every rep ends with a finish.
- The coach calls the trigger: “Drag!”, “He follows!”, “Empty wing!”.

What happens:
Left run: LCB → LDM (drags) → bounce to LB → diagonal into the inverted LW → in behind for the 9.

Link to the game model:
Patterns P2, P3, P4 and P5.

items.text:
RIGHT RUN
RCB → RB → RW → RDM →
the 10 in the empty
wing.

steps.title: T3 Pattern runs · Unopposed to live — The right run (P4)
steps.note:
What happens:
Right run: RCB → RB → into the dropping RW → set to the RDM → the 10 into the empty wing → cutback.

Coaching points:
- Passes on the ground, firm, into the far foot.
- Every set is first time on an angle.
- Runs start as the pass before travels.

Progressions:
- Swap in P5 (the 10 drops, drives and sprints) and P6 (up, back, through).

items.text:
STAGES
Walk · match speed ·
passive · live.

steps.title: T3 Pattern runs · Unopposed to live — Stages and coaching
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Timing beats speed: arrive into the space as the pass before is played.
- Same rules as the game: a man on your back, set on an angle.

Progressions:
- Stage 2: match speed, the coach times each rep (aim: under 10 s from the first pass to the finish).
- Stage 3: passive red players replace the mannequins and choose whether to jump; blue read the trigger.
- Stage 4: live defenders; red win the ball and counter to the halfway line.

Dose:
20 min in total.

items.text:
T4 · PROGRESS FROM THE RIGHT
10 v 8 + GK. 3 points
for a goal from the
right.

steps.title: T4 Phase of play · Progress from the right — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- From our half to their goal. 10 blue (back four, DLPs, wingers, 10, 9) against 8 red (back four, midfield four) and their goalkeeper.
- Two mini goals on the halfway line for red. Each rep starts with the coach’s pass to a blue centre-back.
- 4 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

Rules:
- Blue: free touches. The fullbacks start deep and wide. The 9 starts on a blind side.
- Red win the ball: they attack the mini goals; blue counter-press for 5 seconds.

Scoring:
- Blue goal: 1. Goal after the ball went into the 10 or the RW on the right, facing forward: 3.
- Red: mini goal 1; a regain in their own half that reaches the halfway line 1.

Link to the game model:
Identity 5 (progress from the right), patterns P4, P5, P7, non-negotiable 7.

items.text:
READ IT
Their fullback follows
the RW: the wing is
empty.

steps.title: T4 Phase of play · Progress from the right — Read the right side
steps.note:
What happens:
The ball goes to the right-back; their wide midfielder jumps him. Our RW drops and their fullback follows. The 10 now chooses: the empty wing (P4) or the drop (P5).

Coaching points:
- The 10 reads their fullback before he moves.
- The RDM is the hinge: close and diagonal to the RB.

Questions to ask:
- Their fullback followed the RW: where is the space?
- Nobody followed the 10: what now?

items.text:
EMPTY WING
RB → RW → RDM → the 10.
Goal: 3 points.

steps.title: T4 Phase of play · Progress from the right — Into the empty wing: 3 points on
steps.note:
What happens:
RB into the RW, set to the RDM, the 10 into the empty wing. A goal from here scores 3.

Coaching points:
- Each set first time on an angle.
- The 10 attacks the byline; the 9, the LW and the RW fill the box.

items.text:
PROGRESSIONS
Strikers on · 8 passes ·
press on call.

steps.title: T4 Phase of play · Progress from the right — Progressions
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Engine: one deep, one wide, one inside, one between the lines.
- Rest defence: two centre-backs, one DLP and the far fullback stay behind the ball.

Progressions:
- Add their two strikers: 10 v 10 + GK, starting from our goalkeeper.
- Blue limited to 8 passes before a shot.
- Red may switch to a high press on the coach’s call.

Regressions:
- Red fullbacks always follow our wingers.
- Red midfield passive for the first two passes.

Dose:
4 x 6 min, 2 min rest.

items.text:
T5 · POSSESSION ON PURPOSE
11 v 11 with bonuses for
our identity.

steps.title: T5 Game · Possession on purpose — Set-up
steps.note:
Organisation:
- 11 v 11 between the boxes and the halfway line, or on a full pitch. Normal rules.
- 2 x 12 min, 3 min rest. The opponent plays the system of next match’s opponent.

Rules:
- Our 9 may never stand between their centre-backs: the coach stops play and gives the ball away if he does.

Scoring:
- Goal: 1.
- Bonus +1: the attack came through a free player receiving facing forward in a half-space or the centre.
- Bonus +1: the attack went through the right side (RB, RDM, RW or the 10) before the final pass.
- Bonus +1: ball won back within 5 seconds of losing it, in their half.

Link to the game model:
The whole model: draw, find, face forward, accelerate, and win it back.

items.text:
COACH THE GAME
Freeze for the non-
negotiables, praise the
purpose.

steps.title: T5 Game · Possession on purpose — Coaching the game
steps.note:
Coaching points:
- Freeze only for the non-negotiables: the box, the bodies, the 9’s position, the rest defence.
- Praise the pass that draws as loudly as the pass that scores.
- Count the bonuses aloud: the players learn what we value.

Questions to ask:
- Where was the free man?
- Which pass drew them?
- Did we go within two passes?
